title: Thompson (1917) On Growth and Form, Ch. IX 'On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons' — radial deposition of calcospherites about a centre (Harting 1872 artificial concretions in egg albumen)
claim: Concretions and calcospherites grow by radial deposition about a centre (Harting's artificial concretions in egg albumen mimic natural ones), giving concentric/spherical forms by physical deposition alone.

source.citation: Thompson, D'Arcy W. (1917) On Growth and Form. Cambridge University Press, 1st ed., Ch. IX pp. 411-487, Figs. 194-235

primary_experimental_source.citation: Harting, P. (1872) Recherches de morphologie synthétique sur la production artificielle de quelques formations calcaires organiques. Verh. K. Akad. Wet. Amsterdam 13:1-84
primary_experimental_source.method_as_quoted_by_thompson_p421: bring some soluble salt of lime, such as the chloride or nitrate, into solution within a colloid medium, such as gum, gelatine or albumin; and then to precipitate it out in the form of some insoluble compound, such as the carbonate or oxalate

state_variables.R: radius of the spherite front from its nucleus (length)
state_variables.rho(theta,t): radial distance of the front in direction theta (2-D section); asphericity A = (max rho - min rho)/mean rho
state_variables.a(r,t), b(r,t): concentrations of the inner (CaCl2 / AgNO3) and outer (Na2CO3 / K2Cr2O7) electrolytes in the colloid
state_variables.p(r,t): precipitate (CaCO3 / Ag2CrO4) density; bands = local maxima of p(r) at the end of the run
state_variables.r_n: radius of the n-th concentric band (lamella) counted from the nucleus
state_variables.phi(x,y): quasi-static Laplacian supply field around a growing 2-D cluster (dielectric-breakdown-model surrogate for diffusion-limited supply)
state_variables.eta: supply exponent of the dielectric-breakdown model: growth probability of a perimeter site is proportional to |grad phi|^eta (eta = 0 interface-controlled Eden growth, eta = 1 diffusion-limited aggregation, eta > 1 strongly supply-starved)

E1_interface_controlled_radial_depositio.formula: dR/dt = v  =>  R(t) = R_0 + v t;  lamella thickness delta_n = R_{n+1} - R_n = v*Delta t = const
E1_interface_controlled_radial_depositio.source: Thompson p. 421-422 & 437 (deposition 'about some minute point or centre'); Keith & Padden 1963 / Hoffman & Lauritzen 1961 linear spherulite growth

E2_diffusion_limited_radial_deposition.formula: R dR/dt = D Omega (c_inf - c_eq) = kappa  =>  R(t)^2 = R_0^2 + 2 kappa t;  (R_{n+1}-R_n)(R_{n+1}+R_n) = 2 kappa Delta t  =>  lamellae thin outward
E2_diffusion_limited_radial_deposition.source: Zener (1949) / Frank (1950) quasi-steady diffusion to a sphere; Mullins & Sekerka (1963)

E3_sphericity_stability_under_uniform_no.formula: rho(theta,t) = rho_0(theta) + v t  =>  max rho - min rho = const,  A(t) = (max rho_0 - min rho_0)/(mean rho_0 + v t) -> 0
E3_sphericity_stability_under_uniform_no.source: Huygens/eikonal front propagation; Thompson p. 425-426 (rounded contours)

E4_equal_rate_impingement_plane.formula: |x - c_1|^2 - |x - c_2|^2 = 2 (c_2 - c_1) . x + |c_1|^2 - |c_2|^2  (affine in x)  =>  two spherites nucleated simultaneously and growing at equal rate meet on the perpendicular-bisector plane; N centres give a Voronoi mosaic with mean 6 neighbours in 2-D
E4_equal_rate_impingement_plane.source: Thompson p. 422 (polyhedral, often regularly hexagonal outlines when crowded), p. 426 (contiguous soap-bubbles)

E5_liesegang_supersaturation_banding.formula: da/dt = D_a Lap_r a - Rp,  db/dt = D_b Lap_r b - Rp,  dp/dt = Rp;  Rp = k (ab - K_sp)_+ [H(p - 0) + H(ab - K_ss)];  Lap_r = r^-2 d/dr (r^2 d/dr);  bands at r_n with r_{n+1}/r_n -> P (Jablczynski spacing coefficient), r_n^2 ~ t_n
E5_liesegang_supersaturation_banding.source: Thompson p. 427 ('stand farther and farther apart, in logarithmic ratio, as they recede from the centre'); Ostwald (1897) supersaturation theory; Jablczynski (1923); Matalon & Packter (1955); Antal, Droz, Magnin, Racz & Zrinyi (1998)

E6_dielectric_breakdown_supply_sweep.formula: Lap phi = 0 outside cluster, phi = 0 on cluster, phi = 1 on far boundary;  P(grow at perimeter site i) = |grad phi_i|^eta / sum_j |grad phi_j|^eta
E6_dielectric_breakdown_supply_sweep.source: Niemeyer, Pietronero & Wiesmann (1984); Witten & Sander (1981); Eden (1961); Thompson p. 424 (scanty supply -> spinous/digitiform outgrowths)

boundary_and_initial_conditions.E1_E2: R(0) = R_0 > 0; seed may be aspherical (rho_0(theta) = R_0 (1 + eps cos(m theta)) or a square nucleus)
boundary_and_initial_conditions.E5: a(r <= r_0, t) = a_0 (inner reservoir, Dirichlet); a(r_max,t) = 0 (far field); b(r,0) = b_0 for r > r_0; zero-flux for b at r = 0 and r = r_max; p(r,0) = 0
boundary_and_initial_conditions.E6: single seed site at the grid centre; phi = 1 on a circle of radius R_launch = R_cluster + 8 lattice units; growth stopped at N_sites

parameter_regimes.expected: compact, near-circular cluster, circularity > 0.8, mass-radius exponent ~ 2.0
branched aggregate, mass-radius exponent ~ 1.7, low circularity
parameter_regimes.thompson_text: when the albumin was somewhat scanty ... spheroidal globules tended to become rough, by an outgrowth of spinous or digitiform projections (p. 424)

liesegang_parameters.control_no_threshold: K_ss = K_sp (no supersaturation gap) -> continuous deposit, no discrete bands

empirical_reference_values.note: r_{n+1}/r_n for Liesegang bands, system-dependent; approaches 1 for large a_0/b_0 (Matalon-Packter)

empirical_biological_claims_from_text.test: CV of boundary radius about the centroid of Fig. 196 spherite; radial-profile ring count; radial fibre alignment in Carmel ooids

empirical_biological_claims_from_text.claim: crowded calcospherites assume polyhedral, often regularly hexagonal outlines
empirical_biological_claims_from_text.test: neighbour count and area CV of segmented Fig. 197 mosaic vs equal-rate Voronoi simulation

empirical_biological_claims_from_text.claim: with scanty albumin / scanty supply the globules become rough with spinous or digitiform projections
empirical_biological_claims_from_text.test: eta sweep: circularity and mass-radius exponent collapse from Eden (eta=0) to DLA (eta>=1)

empirical_biological_claims_from_text.claim: concentric zones stand farther and farther apart, in logarithmic ratio, as they recede from the centre (Liesegang)
empirical_biological_claims_from_text.test: geometric vs arithmetic fit of band radii in the Liesegang specimen and in the E5 simulation; spacing coefficient P

empirical_biological_claims_from_text.test: ring count & concentricity on Fig. 209 plaice otoliths (qualitative, plate only)

empirical_biological_claims_from_text.test: all radial models seeded from a point nucleus; asphericity decay exponent ~ -1 vs R
